cards.explanation: The answer is that Paul commends them for remembering him and keeping the traditions he passed on. He says, “Now I commend you for remembering me in everything and for maintaining the traditions, just as I passed them on to you.” That's a double compliment: they remembered him, and they kept what he handed down. If somebody told me I was remembered in EVERYTHING, I'd need to sit down on this gold base for a minute.

The answer is Christ. Paul says, “…the head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is man…” So Christ is the head named for every man. Notice he's laying out a line of heads here, and he's about to add one more.
The answer is God. Paul finishes the list with “…the head of Christ is God.” That's the last of the three heads he names. I like how he lines them up so clearly, step by step.

The answer is that he dishonors his head. Paul says, “Every man who prays or prophesies with his head covered dishonors his head.” He starts with the man, and in the very next verse he turns to the woman. Hold onto that word dishonors, friends, because it comes back.

The answer is False. Paul says a woman who prays or prophesies with her head uncovered “…dishonors her head…” The word is dishonors, not honors. Read it carefully, friends, because that one word makes all the difference.
The answer is cover. Paul says, “…she should cover her head.” It comes right after he says that if it's shameful for a woman to have her hair cut or shaved off. The word is cover, plain and simple.

The answer is that he is the image and glory of God. Paul says, “A man ought not to cover his head, since he is the image and glory of God…” That's the reason he gives. Then he moves on to the woman, so stay with me, friends.
The answer is True. Paul says, “For man did not come from woman, but woman from man.” That's his reason for what he just said about the woman being the glory of man. Short verse, clear answer.

The answer is the angels. Paul says, “For this reason a woman ought to have a sign of authority on her head, because of the angels.” The phrase is “…because of the angels.” He doesn't explain it further in these verses, so I won't either.

The answer is True. Paul says, “In the Lord, however, woman is not independent of man, nor is man independent of woman.” It goes both ways, and Paul says so himself. That little word “however” turns the corner for him.

The answer is that man is born of woman. Paul says, “For just as woman came from man, so also man is born of woman.” So it goes in both directions, and that matches what he said right before. Then he adds that everything comes from God.

The answer is that he tells them to judge for themselves. Paul says, “Judge for yourselves: Is it proper for a woman to pray to God with her head uncovered?” The command comes first, and then the question. He hands it to them to weigh.

The answer is False. Paul asks if nature teaches that “…if a man has long hair, it is a disgrace to him…” The glory belongs to the woman, he says: “…if a woman has long hair, it is her glory?” Notice who gets which, friends.
The answer is covering. Paul says, “For long hair is given to her as a covering.” That's the reason he gives for calling it her glory. He ties it all together in that one word.

The answer is that Paul says he and the churches of God have no other practice. He writes, “If anyone is inclined to dispute this, we have no other practice, nor do the churches of God.” He points to what he and the churches of God do. It's his closing word on the whole subject.
